meta.title: Free Consulting Agreement Template (Advisory Services) | Workmatic
meta.description: Download a free Consulting Agreement template for advisory services. Covers scope, fees, expenses, IP ownership, confidentiality, and liability cap. For consultants who advise — not implement.

subtitle: A professional starting-point template for advisory consulting engagements. Covers advisory scope, fee structure, expense reimbursement, IP ownership, and liability limitation. For consultants who advise — not implement.

key_clauses_to_watch.title: Scope of Engagement
key_clauses_to_watch.why_it_matters: Advisory scope must be distinct from operational execution. Define deliverables as reports, recommendations, analyses — not implementation.

key_clauses_to_watch.title: Fee Structure
key_clauses_to_watch.why_it_matters: Choose: hourly, daily, project-based, or retainer. Retainers should define scope cap and rollover terms. Avoid open-ended time commitments.

key_clauses_to_watch.title: Expense Reimbursement
key_clauses_to_watch.why_it_matters: Pre-approval required for expenses >$[AMOUNT]. Travel, software, subcontractors — define what's reimbursable and caps.

key_clauses_to_watch.title: Intellectual Property
key_clauses_to_watch.why_it_matters: Consultant retains methodology/framework IP. Client owns deliverables. Critical distinction for repeatable consulting methodologies.

key_clauses_to_watch.title: Confidentiality & Data
key_clauses_to_watch.why_it_matters: Consultants often access sensitive data. Define data handling, return/destruction on termination, and survival period (3-5 years typical).

key_clauses_to_watch.title: Liability Cap
key_clauses_to_watch.why_it_matters: Cap at fees paid (12 months). Carve-outs for IP, confidentiality, fraud. Professional liability insurance requirement often expected.

key_clauses_to_watch.title: Non-Solicitation
key_clauses_to_watch.why_it_matters: Narrow: only personnel directly worked with. 12 months typical. Must be reasonable in geography and scope.

faq.question: What's the difference between consulting and contracting?
faq.answer: Consulting = advisory, strategic, recommendations (reports, analyses). Contracting = execution, deliverables (code, designs, builds). This template is for advisory engagements where you advise but don't implement.

faq.question: Should I use a retainer or project-based fee?
faq.answer: Retainer: predictable revenue, ongoing advisory relationship. Define monthly hour cap, rollover policy (use-it-or-lose-it vs. rollover), and termination notice. Project-based: fixed scope, fixed fee, clearer boundaries.

faq.question: Who owns my consulting methodology?
faq.answer: You do. This template explicitly retains your methodologies, frameworks, tools, and know-how. Client only owns the specific deliverables (reports, presentations, analyses) created for them.

faq.question: Do I need professional liability insurance?
faq.answer: Many clients require it ($1M+ typical). Even if not required, it's prudent for consultants. This template references insurance requirements in Section 9.
